newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares close at record low.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares close at record low.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended at a record closing low on Monday but did not reach the all-time low of 46.731 points thanks to domestic support for Pudong shares late in the session, brokers said.
The index fell 0.301 points or 0.64 percent to 46.880 points, below the previous record closing low of 47.077 points set last Thursday.
Trading volume was 2.9 million shares worth $1.3 million. Of 41 B shares, 27 traded with 12 down nine flat and six up.

Brokers said few investors were paying attention to the market due to its long-term bearish performance, and only a small amount of domestic buying in Pudong shares prevented the index from falling below the all-time low of 46.731 points.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development reversed early losses in the afternoon, ending unchanged at $0.880 on volume of 570,700 shares.
"Sluggish trading has made the market easy for buyers but difficult sellers, which has dampened the interest of overesas investors greatly," a broker said.
"Liquidation will contiune in the short term," a second broker said. "Given the current situation, it would not be surprising to see the index hit 40 points if there is no positive news."
Shanghai Industrial Sewing Machine was the biggest loser on unwinding selling due to its poor results, plunging $0.016 or 13.33 percent to $0.104 on volume of 317,000 shares.

Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere traded the most on liquidation triggered by its plan to offer another 100 million B shares, brokers said. It fell $0.004 or 0.84 percent to $0.470 on volume of 1.0 million shares.
Shanghai A shares rose on a technical rebound after falls over the past few days, but most investors remained cautious about following up, brokers said.

The A index rose 15.517 points or 1.58 percent to 994.687 points on volume of 396.5 million shares worth 3.7 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index gained 28.652 points or 1.16 percent to 2488.646 points.
Liaoyuan Deheng was the star on speculative buying, soaring 0.61 yuan or 13.09 percent to 5.27 yuan on volume of 6.1 million shares.
